paper.title: Adaptive Partitioning Schemes for Optimistic Optimization

settings.name_in_paper: Deterministic black-box optimization of multi-index functions f(x)=g(Ax) on [-1,1]^d with a budget of n evaluations (simple regret)
unmapped: Domain X=[-1,1]^d (hypercube), single fixed deterministic function, maximization
Multi-index structure f(x)=g(Ax) with A in R^{m x d} having orthonormal rows, m<d, g Lipschitz

Local smoothness w.r.t. a hierarchical partition (Assumption 2.6 of Bartlett et al.: f(x) >= f* - nu rho^h on the optimal cell at depth h); difficulty measured by near-optimality dimension eta_P of the default trisection partition
Fixed budget of n evaluations; regret is simple regret f* - f(x_hat(n))
settings.definition_quote: We consider the problem of optimizing a function $f \colon \mathcal{X} \mapsto \RR$ using only its evaluations at appropriately chosen points in its domain $\mathcal{X}$... Given a budget of $n$ evaluations, at each $t$ the algorithm queries a point $\vec{x}_t$ and observes a real number $y_t = f(\vec{x}_t)$. After exhausting its budget, the algorithm returns the estimated maximizer $\hat{\vec{x}}(n)$. ... simple regret $r_n \triangleq f^* - f(\hat{\vec{x}}(n))$. ... multi-index functions ... $f(\vec{x}) = g(\vec{A} \vec{x})$.

algorithms.name: SequOOL on learned partitioning scheme (Algorithm 1 + SequOOL, two-stage)
SequOOL on an adaptive partitioning scheme with lookahead direction selection (Algorithm 2, interleaved)

symbols.rho: local smoothness rate of the default partition (Assumption 2.6)
symbols.nu: local smoothness scale of the default partition
symbols.h_2: m + m*ceil(log_3(2 sqrt(m) kappa_2/(kappa_2-1))), kappa_2 = sqrt(m)/sqrt(1-dist^2(A, A_hat))
symbols.C_1: 3^d d^{d-m} (12 sqrt(m))^m C rho^{-eta_P h_3} 4^m rho^{eta_P h_4}
symbols.l_f: f* - inf over kappa_1 H^d of f
symbols.l_g: g* - inf over kappa_2 alpha H^m of g(A A_hat^T z)

conditions: f is a multi-index function f(x)=g(Ax) with A having orthonormal rows, m<d
default partition satisfies Assumption 2.6 with (nu, rho) and near-optimality dimension eta_P = 0 with constant C

source.label: thm:main_theorem_1
source.quote: For a function in the multi-index class \eqref{eq:multi_index_model}, the regret of SequOOL applied on the partitioning scheme using $\hat{\vec{A}}$ returned by Algorithm~\ref{alg:svd_partitioning} and $\hat{\alpha} = \sqrt{dm}/\sqrt{1- \dist^2(\Vec{A}, \hat{\Vec{A}})}$ satisfies r_n \leq \gamma(\nu, \rho) \rho^{-\beta\tilde{h}_2 } \rho^{\frac{\beta}{C_1} {\lfloor\frac{n}{\overline{\log n}}\rfloor}} if \eta_{\mathcal{P}} = 0 ...

results.notes: Paper's n is T. Deterministic evaluations; bound holds given A_hat (which comes from randomized first stage); recorded as almost_sure. The samples used by Algorithm 1 to learn A_hat are not counted in n. Table 1 summarises as rho^{beta Omega~(n)}.

symbols.rho: local smoothness rate of the default partition
symbols.C_1: 3^d d^{d-m} (12 sqrt(m))^m C rho^{-eta_P h_3} 4^m rho^{eta_P h_4}

conditions: f is a multi-index function f(x)=g(Ax) with A having orthonormal rows, m<d
default partition satisfies Assumption 2.6 with (nu, rho) and near-optimality dimension eta_P > 0 with constant C
results.notes: Paper summarises as r_n = O~(n^{-beta/eta_P}) vs O~(n^{-1/eta_P}) for default SequOOL. Paper's n is T.
